gloss: Issun-bōshi; the One-Inch Boy (folk tale character)

definitions.explanation: A character from a famous Japanese folk tale — a tiny boy the size of one sun (about 3 cm) who goes on adventures and eventually grows to full size after defeating an ogre.

definitions.gloss: a very small person; a tiny person
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively to refer to someone extremely short or small in stature.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}に{一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}の{話|はなし}を{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I read the story of Issun-bōshi to the children.

examples.japanese: {一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}は{針|はり}を{刀|かたな}にして{鬼|おに}と{戦|たたか}った。
examples.english: Issun-bōshi used a needle as his sword and fought the ogre.

examples.japanese: {一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}は{日本|にほん}の{代表的|だいひょうてき}な{昔話|むかしばなし}の{一|ひと}つで、{小|ちい}さくても{勇気|ゆうき}があれば{大|おお}きなことを{成|な}し{遂|と}げられるという{教訓|きょうくん}がある。
examples.english: Issun-bōshi is one of Japan's classic folk tales, carrying the lesson that even someone small can achieve great things with courage.

examples.japanese: うちの{弟|おとうと}は{一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}みたいに{小|ちい}さい。
examples.english: My little brother is tiny, like Issun-bōshi.

examples.japanese: {背|せ}が{低|ひく}いので{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}から{一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}と{呼|よ}ばれていた。
examples.english: Because I was short, I was called Issun-bōshi since childhood.

examples.japanese: {一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}のような{体格|たいかく}でも、{柔道|じゅうどう}では{誰|だれ}にも{負|ま}けなかった。
examples.english: Even with a tiny build like Issun-bōshi, he never lost to anyone in judo.

notes:
The name literally means "one-sun monk/boy," where {一寸|いっすん} is an old unit of measurement equal to about 3.03 centimeters, and {法師|ほうし} means a Buddhist monk or, in folk tales, a boy or small person.

The tale is part of the {御伽草子|おとぎぞうし} collection from the Muromachi period. In the story, an elderly childless couple prays for a child and receives a boy no bigger than a thumb. Despite his size, he travels to the capital, serves a noble family, defeats an {鬼|おに} (ogre), and obtains the {打|う}ち{出|で}の{小槌|こづち} (magic mallet), which grants his wish to become full-sized. The story is often compared to Western tales like Tom Thumb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}の{話|はなし}: the tale of Issun-bōshi
- {一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}みたいに{小|ちい}さい: tiny like Issun-bōshi

RELATED TERMS:
- {昔話|むかしばなし}: folk tale
- {桃太郎|ももたろう}: Momotarō (Peach Boy, another famous folk tale hero)
- {打|う}ち{出|で}の{小槌|こづち}: magic mallet (the treasure obtained in the story)
